evals.prompt: I want to create a new skill called 'code-review' that helps review pull requests. Can you scaffold it for me?
evals.expected_output: A new skill directory at the appropriate location with SKILL.md, frontmatter, and basic structure
assertions: The skill directory is created with a SKILL.md file
The SKILL.md has proper YAML frontmatter with name and description
The description includes trigger phrases and negative triggers

evals.prompt: My skill's description is too vague. It says 'Helps with data visualization.' Can you fix it?
evals.expected_output: A refined description that specifies what the skill does, when to use it, and key capabilities
assertions: The new description is more specific than the original
The description includes what the skill does and when to use it

evals.prompt: I have a skill that runs shell commands to deploy infrastructure. It has too much inline code in the SKILL.md. Can you help me restructure it?
evals.expected_output: A refactored skill that moves shell logic to scripts/ and keeps SKILL.md focused on workflow and guidance
assertions: The SKILL.md is shorter and focuses on workflow rather than inline code
The scripts/ directory contains the shell logic
The skill follows CLI-first design patterns

evals.prompt: Create a new skill called 'deploy-staging' that wraps a shell script to deploy to staging. Include evals for it.
evals.expected_output: A new skill with SKILL.md, a scripts/deploy.sh, and evals/evals.json with 2-3 test cases
assertions: The skill directory is created with SKILL.md, scripts/, and evals/
evals/evals.json has at least 2 test cases with prompts and assertions
The SKILL.md includes an Evals section describing how to run evals
The eval test cases cover varied prompts (casual and precise)
